card.name: Dabke
card.tagline: Levantine stomping line dance led by a handkerchief-waving lawweeh
card.profile: Dabke is the Levantine folk line dance performed at weddings and celebrations across Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Palestine and Iraq (Wikipedia). Dancers link hands in a line or semicircle and stamp and jump in synchronised six-beat patterns; the line is led by a lawweeh (raas) who waves a handkerchief or string of beads (masbaha), improvising leaps and breaks (Wikipedia; iHeritage). The name derives from Levantine Arabic dabaka, 'stamping of the feet'; folklore links its stomping origin to communally tamping mud rooftops (Bayt Al Fann).
card.insight: Though a powerful emblem of Lebanese identity, dabke is shared across the whole Levant and is not uniquely Lebanese. After the launch of the Baalbek International Festival in 1956, Soviet dance expert Igor Moiseyev was invited to assess Lebanese folk traditions and proposed a standardized choreography (The Beiruter; iHeritage).

lessons.teacher_style: The instructor talks directly to the camera to explain origins and counts, then switches to a first-person or side-angle view of his feet to demonstrate the steps. He breaks down each variant step-by-step from slow to regular speed before demonstrating them with music.
lessons.distinctive_method: Using a first-person chest-mounted or downward-facing camera angle on his feet so learners see the exact footwork from their own perspective.
what_works: First-person foot camera angle helps viewers follow foot placement directly
Progression from slow explanation to music practice
what_hinders: Frequent camera angle changes between upper body and feet

observation.setting: A banquet hall or wedding reception venue with tables, chairs, guests seated on the sides, and a polished marble dance floor.
observation.dancers: A group of young men in suits, some holding flags or sticks, joined in a line.
observation.formation_and_space: A line of dancers holding hands or arms linked, moving sideways across the dance floor.
observation.posture: Torso upright, knees bending flexibly with steps, body weight shifting rhythmically.
observation.footwork: Stepping sideways, stamping, crossing feet, and lifting knees high on the beat; fast footwork details obscured by camera motion.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held out and linked or holding hands with neighbors; some dancers wave flags or sticks overhead or clap in unison.
observation.hips_and_torso: Torso remains relatively upright with natural bounciness matching the steps; slight upper body leaning during high kicks.
observation.partnering: Group line formation with hand-to-hand contact or arm links between dancers.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Upright level with energetic jumps, high knee lifts, and simultaneous stomping on the beat.
observation.costume_and_props: Men wearing business suits, dress shirts, and ties; some holding Palestinian flags and decorated sticks.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact foot placement details and precise weight distribution are difficult to see due to wide camera angles and rapid panning.
